rationale.conceptual: The paper provides explicit closed-form algebraic expressions for all indices; the agent only needs to evaluate them. Feature selection and regression use standard libraries in a commonplace way. No novel algorithm or deep domain expertise is required to implement.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of several sequential steps: generate index values for 10,000 cells, compute HOF, normalize, run exhaustive feature selection, and train eight regression models. However, all steps are contained in a single Python script with straightforward I/O, no complex tooling or external data fetching.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves computing explicitly given formulas for topological indices (no derivation required), then applying standard off-the-shelf feature selection and regression from scikit-learn and mlxtend. The conceptual difficulty is minimal; execution is a straightforward multi-step script with no heavy orchestration. Resources are negligible as all data is generated from formulas and models are simple.

compute_estimate.reasoning: All data is generated from algebraic formulas; the dataset is tiny (10,000 rows × ~40 columns) and models are simple linear and tree-based regressions. No GPU needed, minimal RAM.
